title: UAEがOPECを脱退　増産志向でサウジ主導の原油減産に不満　ホルムズ封鎖が引き金
extracted_text: アラブ首長国連邦（UAE）は1日、石油輸出国機構（OPEC）を脱退した。OPECにロシアなど非加盟の産油国を加えたOPECプラスからも脱退した。原油生産量の制約をなくし、段階的に増産する狙いがある。UAEは近年、サウジアラビアが原油相場を支えるために主導した減産に不満を抱いていた。エネルギー輸送の要衝ホルムズ海峡の事実上の封鎖が続く中東情勢の悪化が脱退を後押しした。 OPECは原油生産量を調整し価格や供給の安定化を図る。生産調整で原油の国際価格に大きな影響を与えてきたが、主要産油国であるUAEの脱退で価格支配力の低下は避けられない。 UAEは脱退声明で「われわれは多大な貢献と、それ以上に大きな犠牲を払ってきた」と主張した。OPEC最大の産油量を持つサウジは歳入の大半を石油収入に依存し、原油価格を下げないよう生産量抑制を重視してきた。一方、UAEは増産してより多くの石油を売ることを志向し、サウジ主導のOPECが各国に生産枠を割り当てる減産に不満を募らせていた。 UAE脱退の引き金となったのは、米イスラエルとイランとの交戦に伴うホルムズ海峡の事実上の封鎖だ。OPECプラスの一部の国々は4月からの増産を決めたが、海峡封鎖で原油を搬出できず、UAEの3月の生産量は交戦前に当たる2月と比べ大幅に減少した。 状況打開のため、UAEはホルムズ海峡を通らずに搬出できる輸送ルートとして、UAE東部のオマーン湾岸のフジャイラ港の活用を模索する。英BBC放送によると、同港では既に原油を運ぶパイプラインが使用されており、増産に備えて増強が必要とされている。 イラン情勢で原油価格は高騰し、世界的な脱炭素化の動きを背景に需要の縮小も想定される。UAEには原油価格が高止まりするうちに売りさばきたいとの思惑もある。（岡田美月）
translated_text: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) withdrew from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) on the 1st. It also withdrew from OPEC+, which includes non-member oil-producing nations such as Russia. The move aims to remove restrictions on crude oil production and gradually increase output. In recent years, the UAE had been dissatisfied with the production cuts led by Saudi Arabia to support the oil market. The deteriorating Middle East situation, including the de facto blockade of the Hormuz Strait - a key route for energy transport - accelerated the withdrawal. OPEC adjusts crude oil production to stabilize prices and supply. It has significantly influenced international oil prices through production adjustments, but the loss of the UAE, a major oil-producing country, will inevitably diminish its pricing power. In its withdrawal statement, the UAE claimed, "We have made tremendous contributions and even greater sacrifices." Saudi Arabia, which has the largest oil production quota in OPEC, relies most of its national revenue on oil income and has prioritized production restraint to keep crude prices high. Meanwhile, the UAE has sought to produce and sell more oil, growing increasingly dissatisfied with the production quota allocations imposed by Saudi Arabia-led OPEC. The trigger for the UAE's withdrawal was the de facto blockade of the Hormuz Strait as fighting between the US/Israel and Iran intensified. Some OPEC+ countries decided to increase production starting in April, but the strait blockade prevented crude oil exports, causing the UAE's March production to drop significantly compared to February, before the fighting began. To break the deadlock, the UAE is exploring the use of Fujairah Port on the Omani Gulf coast in eastern UAE as an export route that bypasses the Hormuz Strait. According to the BBC, pipelines are already in use at the port to transport crude oil, and capacity needs to be strengthened in preparation for increased output. Iran-related tensions have driven oil prices higher, while global decarbonization efforts are expected to reduce demand. The UAE also seeks to sell as much oil as possible while prices remain elevated. (Mitsuki Okada)
title_en: UAE Withdraws from OPEC Amid Push to Increase Output, Dissatisfied with Saudi-Led Production Cuts; Hormuz Blockade Triggered Exit
